Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

distance noun

the space between two places or things

also at a distance, from a distance, at an equal distance, keep one’s distance, how far apart, interval, gap

classical

Caes. B.G. 1.43.1: aequum ferē spatium … aberat
Ov. M. 8.794: viae spatium, the length of the way (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 203, 305

spatium, spatiī n.

noun, second declension

distance, space; a stretch of road or time

Room, space, and so the distance between two points; also a span of time (spatium vītae). Latin often says how far with the verb abesse and an accusative or ablative of the distance: mīlia passuum tria abest (see away, and how far).

Other words

  • 1intervallum: a left unmarked. Lewis & Short marks neither vallum nor intervallum, and de Vaan (s.v. vallum) reconstructs *walso- without ruling on the vowel. The loci collection prints intervāllō in Liv. 22.12.8; the length is not settled here.

    intervallum1, intervallī n. — the distance between, an interval; a gap in time

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Caes. B.G. 1.43.2: parī intervallō; Liv. 23.29: quīnque mīlium intervallō (Lewis & Short)

    Properly the space between two palisades (inter vallōs); the gap between things in a row, and between moments. From a distance: ex intervallō (Liv.).

Examples

  • Hic locus aequum ferē spatium ā castrīs Ariovistī et Caesaris aberat.

    This place was about the same distance from the camps of Ariovistus and of Caesar.Caes. B.G. 1.43.1

  • Item equitēs Ariovistī parī intervallō cōnstitērunt.

    Ariovistus’ horsemen likewise halted at the same distance.Caes. B.G. 1.43.2

See also far, how far is it?, away, length, equal.
